issue: The PRD requires "merge → resolve → ref-delete runs inside the 00162 write lease"; it does not. `import_bundle` takes the lock three separate times (`merge_remote`, `commit_merge`, `delete_remote_ref`) with unlocked windows between, and `unbundle_git_objects` writes git objects and `refs/remotes/bundle/*` fully outside the lock.
reason: Design-accepted, recorded in the 00168 design doc Risks section: the two-lock-acquisition gap is the exact gap the already-shipped network sync() path has lived with since 00163, so bundle import inherits an identical, already-accepted risk profile rather than a new one. Bob raised the same point and himself filed the unbundle/fetch leg as KNOWN (explicitly deferred by the design as a side-ref-only preparation leg outside 00168's master merge→resolve→ref-delete scope). Collapsing three re-entrant lock acquisitions into one outer lease is a sync-wide change, not a bundle-import change — it belongs to its own PRD.

reason: Pre-existing FFI signature, explicitly out of scope in the 00168 design doc ("FFI's import_bundle binding returns SyncReport today and after this change — no signature change downstream, only field values become more honest"). Widening the FFI return type is a public-interface change requiring the compatibility/deprecation review AGENTS.md mandates; it is a separate PRD, not a rework item. Real gap, tracked at batch end.

issue: `validate_clean_merge_or_fallback` — named by the PRD at `:538-544` as a site that must "stop reporting false success" — is untouched and still `return Ok(0)` when `commit_parent_count < 2` (mod.rs:561).
reason: Requirements-vs-design reconciliation. The PRD named this site because, under the OLD CLI-merge design, a conflicted merge produced no commit and this early return was what manufactured the false Ok(0). Under the chosen design there is no CLI merge: conflicts arrive as MergeResult::Conflicts and never reach this branch, so the false-success path the PRD describes no longer exists. Changing the shared network-sync clean-merge validator to hard-fail on a <2-parent commit would alter network sync behavior outside this PRD's scope.

issue: `map_err(|e| DoogatError::Sync(...))` collapses every resolver error, including the retryable `DoogatError::Conflict` that `with_write_lock` returns on lock-acquire timeout and that `commit_merge`'s divergence guard returns; a lock timeout inside `merge_remote` (line 120, unwrapped) still surfaces as `Conflict`, so the same failure reports two different classes depending on where it lands. Preserve `Conflict` and wrap only the rest.
reason: PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED BY DESIGN, settled in cycle-1 rework task [D1-3] (commits 01cfc85, 427f920). The substantive defect -- one failure reporting two different classes depending on which call raised it -- IS fixed: both `merge_remote` and `apply_merge_result` now route through the same `bundle_merge_error`. The literal remedy ('preserve Conflict and wrap only the rest') was deliberately NOT implemented, because its premise is false in this codebase. `DoogatError::Conflict` is overloaded: retryable producers are write_lock.rs:72 (lock-acquire timeout) and git_ops/merge.rs:65 (resolve->commit window guard); TERMINAL producers are git_ops/merge.rs:193 (collision loser whose id cannot be rewritten) and sync_manager/mod.rs:502 (binary conflict missing blob OID). Preserving Conflict was implemented first and empirically broke three tests -- conflicting_bundle_import_leaves_repo_clean_on_merge_failure, conflicting_bundle_import_leaves_bundle_ref_reachable_on_merge_failure, and kept_bundle_ref_survives_a_later_import_under_fetch_prune (the regression test for THIS cycle's CRITICAL finding) -- all of which require the terminal collision failure to be reported as `Sync`, which is also the PRD's documented contract. Both classes can arrive through either wrapped call, so they cannot be distinguished at the import boundary without string-sniffing the message (exactly what this PRD removed). Pat (per-task reviewer) independently checked the evidence chain and concurred. DO NOT re-raise 'Conflict is still collapsed' in a later cycle: that is the settled, deliberate outcome.

issue: `DoogatError::Conflict` is overloaded across a retryable class (write-lock acquire timeout at write_lock.rs:72; the resolve->commit window guard at git_ops/merge.rs:65) and a terminal class (collision loser whose id cannot be rewritten at git_ops/merge.rs:193; binary conflict missing its blob OID at sync_manager/mod.rs:502). A caller that retries on the public CONFLICT category will therefore spin forever on a malformed doogat, and bundle import must now report retryable lock timeouts as `Sync`/Internal to keep the terminal case honest.
reason: NEW finding, discovered during cycle-1 rework task [D1-3] (not raised by any cycle-1 reviewer). Real latent bug, but out of scope for this PRD: `Conflict` maps to a public `CONFLICT` code and `AppErrorCategory::Conflict` (app_contract/error.rs:88), so reclassifying the terminal producers is a public error-shape change requiring the compatibility/deprecation review AGENTS.md mandates, and it touches the shared network-sync resolver rather than bundle import. Needs its own PRD. The tradeoff it forces on bundle import is recorded durably in the CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` bundle entry and in the `bundle_merge_error` doc comment.
